title: Jack Parsons' first Caltech rocket tests

tellings.quote: The original godfather of American rocketry, Jack Parsons, believed this as well. In 1936, he and some colleagues at Caltech began launching the first rocket tests in western Pasadena.
Back in 1936, while Jack Parsons was still testing rockets in the Arroyo Seco, his team managed their first successful liquid fuel test on Halloween night.
tellings.difference: Dates the first successful liquid-fuel test to Halloween night and reads it as a Samhain ritual date.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell of Jack Parsons' first rocket tests in 1936 in western Pasadena (the Arroyo Seco).

as_told.title: Parsons' first liquid-fuel test on Samhain

plain: In 1936 Jack Parsons, whom Michels calls the godfather of American rocketry, began launching the first rocket tests with colleagues from Caltech, a university in Pasadena, California, out in the Arroyo Seco canyon in western Pasadena. Michels tells it himself, without naming a source, and in one episode adds that the team's first successful liquid-fuel test came on Halloween night, which he reads as the date of Samhain, an old pagan festival. He tells it to link the start of American rocketry with ritual and belief.
